questions.q: What grain should the fact table use in this project, and why?
options: One row per order line, because the Operations Manager needs to slice by product
One row per order, because it's simpler to build
One row per territory, because that's the smallest table
One row per month, to keep the table short
questions.explain: Aggregating up to the order level first would lose the ability to slice by product, which the Operations Manager explicitly needs.

questions.q: Why can't this project reuse the Beginner project's approach of one giant flat joined query?
options: Two pages need different slices of the same facts, and DAX time intelligence needs a real Date table
Flat queries are not allowed in T-SQL
AdventureWorks2012 doesn't support joins
A flat query would run too fast
questions.explain: A flat, pre-joined result forces re-filtering on text columns and can't support a proper Date table for time intelligence the way a modeled star schema can.

questions.q: Why does the fact view carry TerritoryID and ProductID instead of TerritoryName and ProductName?
options: So the relationships to the dimension tables are real joins the model uses, not just decoration
Because SQL Server doesn't allow text columns in views
Because names take up more storage than keys
It doesn't matter either way
questions.explain: Keeping only keys in the fact and names in the dimensions means every slice-by-region or slice-by-subcategory visual actually depends on the model's relationships.

questions.q: How many dimension tables does this project's architecture use, and why that number?
options: Two (Product and Territory), plus a Date table — exactly what the two stakeholders' requirements call for
Ten, to future-proof the model
Zero — everything stays in one flat table
One, because only one stakeholder matters
questions.explain: The architecture is deliberately a small star: only the dimensions the actual requirements call for, nothing added just in case.

questions.q: What does marking a table as the model's 'date table' in Power BI enable?
options: DAX time intelligence functions like DATEADD, used for things like week-over-week comparisons
Automatic currency conversion
Faster T-SQL query execution on the source database
The ability to rename columns in SQL Server
questions.explain: A properly marked date table is what DAX time intelligence functions rely on to calculate things like prior-period comparisons correctly.
